note: Rejudged after Dialer.Dial changed (98b534756d and later: the body moved into dialPrepared behind a prepareClientDial backend preparation, descriptors became a clientProtocol owner, and cleanup returns errors). Re-read Section 4.6: 'Max-Failure MUST be configurable, but SHOULD default to five (5) transmissions.' Dial still copies cfg.Timing.LCPMaxFailure into sessionConfig.lcpMaxFailure beside the restart timer and Max-Configure, before negotiateSession, so the configured value still reaches negotiateLCP's Nak counter; the refactor changes only descriptor ownership and cleanup. Section 4.6 counts Configure-Naks sent without sending a Configure-Ack. The tagged units are unchanged. TestConfiguredLCPMaxFailure and TestRFC1661ClientMaxFailureConvertsFurtherNak each exercise configured limits of two and five, require Naks through the limit, and require the next reply to be a Reject carrying the original unacceptable MRU bytes. The server test and TestRFC1661ClientMaxFailureAckRenewsBudget separately require a successful Ack to renew the budget. These assertions distinguish a fixed limit, premature rejection, substituted suggestion bytes and a missing Ack reset. This judgment covers the implemented LCP Configure-Nak senders; it makes no claim about absent IPv6CP counter configuration.
